verdict.rationale: Maritime documents agent-operable provisioning: an idempotent SDK `provision` call, a CLI built for AI agents with `--json` output, and non-interactive key auth. It also offers per-user Linux computers driven by a model and a Files API for reading an agent's disk. However, there is no documented execute-code-and-return-output primitive, and no teardown or delete step, so the full lifecycle is not shown without a human. Missing for 10: explicit code-execution API returning stdout or results, documented sandbox teardown/delete, an end-to-end autonomous lifecycle example, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, my agent can provision its own sandbox, execute code, read the results, and tear it down — end to end without a human

citations.quote: provision is idempotent on it: it returns the existing agent if there is one, else creates a new one.
The Maritime CLI is built to be operated by other AI agents, not just humans: machine-readable output on every command, stable exit codes, and a live self-describing contract.
Authenticate with an env var, never interactively.
The Maritime Files API: eight endpoints and both SDKs to browse, upload, download, and edit an agent's disk over HTTP, even while the agent sleeps.
A persistent Linux desktop (XFCE, Chromium, LibreOffice) for each of _your_ end users, driven by _your_ model.
